note: Pass the block ResourceKey through setId before constructing the Block; construction throws if the id is missing.
Item.Properties#setId is mandatory because the default description id and model are now derived from that key.

from: item name and model implied by the registry id
to: DataComponents.ITEM_NAME and DataComponents.ITEM_MODEL, overridable via Item.Properties#overrideDescription and #overrideModel
note: Set the component or the override when an item must not use its own id for name or model.

from: assets/<ns>/models/item/<name>.json as the only item render definition
to: assets/<ns>/items/<name>.json (Client Items, with a model field) linking to assets/<ns>/models/item/<name>.json
note: Add the items/<name>.json definition or the item falls back to a missing model.
Replace direct NBT reads and writes with ValueInput get* / read and ValueOutput put* / store.
The registry lookup now comes from the ValueInput/ValueOutput context instead of a separate provider argument.
Split removal logic: drop stored contents in preRemoveSideEffects, send neighbour updates in affectNeighborsAfterRemoval.
Container contents are dropped by BlockEntity#preRemoveSideEffects by default.

from: EntityRenderer#render(T entity, float yaw, float partialTick, PoseStack pose, MultiBufferSource buffer, int light)
to: EntityRenderer#submit(T renderState, PoseStack pose, SubmitNodeCollector collector, CameraRenderState camera)
note: Move draw calls into submit* calls on the SubmitNodeCollector and fill a render state in extractRenderState.
The field is private, so every check has to call the method form.
Register a KeyMapping.Category through KeyMapping.Category#register, otherwise the mapping throws when sorted.
Rename every ResourceLocation reference to Identifier, including method names and parameters.
Catch and import the renamed exception type.
Reimport every critereon class from the corrected criterion package.
Most utility classes moved under net.minecraft.util and need new imports.
net.minecraft.client.model and net.minecraft.world.entity were regrouped into per-type subpackages, so reimport all model and entity classes.
Build options through the OptionInstance$Enum constructor with the values and codec instead of implementing OptionEnum.
Ingredients are HolderSet based now, so drop EMPTY and the ItemStack stream factories and use Ingredient#of.
Recipes are registry entries displayed via RecipeDisplay, so move result and icon data into a SlotDisplay.

from: item textures inside the minecraft:blocks atlas
to: a separate minecraft:items atlas, id at AtlasIds#ITEMS
note: Update atlas sources and MaterialMapper use so item sprites come from the items atlas.
GuiItemRenderState takes a TrackingItemRenderState, which tracks the model sources used for the stack.

to: BlockBehaviour#entityInside(BlockState, Level, BlockPos, Entity, boolean intersecting)
note: Update the override signature to take the new boolean telling whether the entity is inside or only intersecting.
Raise the toolchain and IDE to Java 25 before touching any API code.
Replace GuiGraphics everywhere and drop draw, render and submit prefixes plus RenderState suffixes on its methods.
Render methods that submit GUI elements are now extract* calls that fill a render state.
Rename the widget draw override and submit elements instead of drawing them.
The background draw moved up to Screen under a new name.
Follow the extractor naming for the player face helper.

from: LootItemFunctionType (and the other loot *Type wrapper classes)
to: none; BuiltInRegistries.LOOT_FUNCTION_TYPE holds a MapCodec, and getType becomes codec()
note: Register the MapCodec directly and override codec() returning it.

to: none; Entity#interact(Player, InteractionHand, Vec3) receives the hit location
note: Fold interactAt handling into interact, which is now only called inside the interaction range.
The field is protected now, so all callers must use the getter.
ChunkPos is a record now, so swap constructors for the named factories and asLong for pack.

to: none; block and item models go through the feature submission pipeline
note: Replace dispatcher and renderer calls with block model render states and item model submissions.

from: ShapedRecipeBuilder(ItemStack result) and the other builders taking ItemStack
note: Immutability is required in recipes now, so build results from ItemStackTemplate.

to: passing width and height to AbstractContainerScreen(menu, inventory, title, width, height)
note: The fields are final and default to 176x166, so move any assignment into the super call.
Fabric API dropped Yarn names, so the itemgroup package is now creativetab.
Both the helper class and the method were renamed to the Mojang mapping names.
World became Level across Fabric API lifecycle events.
The package moved from world to level and most members were renamed with it.
Same world to level rename on the server lifecycle events.
Data generation output is named after the pack now.
Particle factories are providers in the new naming, including the nested PendingParticleProvider type.
Block render layers are registered per chunk section layer now.
The recipe data-gen sink was renamed alongside the vanilla RecipeOutput.
The client command helper class was renamed, its methods are unchanged.
One BlendFactor enum replaces both sides, with BlendOp naming the merge operation.

from: TextureFormat and the per-element buffer formats of VertexFormatElement
note: Every texture and buffer format is now expressed as a GpuFormat entry such as R8_UNORM.
Both nested enums were promoted to top level types.

to: VertexFormat$Builder#addAttribute(name, GpuFormat) with at most sixteen attributes
note: Build vertex formats attribute by attribute; the fixed element constants are gone.

from: RenderPipeline#UniformDescription and the plain sampler name list
note: Describe samplers and uniforms in a BindGroupLayout instead of on the pipeline.
Gui now owns the current screen, so route screen access through it.
The heads-up display moved into its own Hud object held by Gui.

to: Style#withColor, withBold, withItalic, withUnderlined, withStrikethrough, withObfuscated
note: ChatFormatting was gutted, so express colour and formatting through Style.
Feature rendering now requires a SubmitNodeStorage for the features to submit into.

from: PictureInPictureRenderer constructor taking MultiBufferSource$BufferSource and renderToTexture without a collector
to: constructor without the BufferSource and renderToTexture(state, PoseStack, SubmitNodeCollector)
note: Drop the buffer source parameter and submit elements through the collector.

to: none; StructureProcessor is an interface and getType becomes codec() returning the MapCodec
note: Implement StructureProcessor and register the MapCodec directly.

from: net.minecraft.advancements criteria, triggers and predicates in their old locations
note: Reimport all advancement criteria, trigger and predicate classes.

to: EntitySubPredicate as a functional interface with matches, registered as a Codec
note: Register the predicate Codec, which is now the key of the EntityPredicate map.

to: none; TagsProvider takes the KeyTagProvider tag methods and TagAppender takes ResourceKeys
note: Extend TagsProvider directly and add entries by ResourceKey or TagKey.

from: Items#WHITE_DYE and the other per-colour item fields
note: Colour and weathering variants are grouped into collections, so read entries from the collection.

from: ResourceKeys obtained from the Blocks, Items, EntityTypes, BlockEntityTypes, Fluids and Potions classes
to: BlockIds, ItemIds, EntityTypeIds, BlockEntityTypeIds, FluidIds, PotionIds, and BlockItemIds for blocks with items
note: Take the ResourceKey from the matching Ids class instead of the registry holder.
Vulkan is a supported backend, so do not assume the OpenGL classes exist.
Split float and int providers and register the MapCodec to CONTEXT_FLOAT_PROVIDER_TYPE or CONTEXT_INT_PROVIDER_TYPE.

to: none; criteria instances take a Holder of LootItemCondition instead
note: Replace the wrapper with a Holder-wrapped condition list in trigger instances.

from: BlockStateProviderType, StructurePlacementType and PlacementModifierType with their type accessors
to: none; the registries hold a MapCodec and type becomes codec()
note: Register the MapCodec directly and rename the accessor to codec.

from: Block#codec and the block type MapCodec registry
note: Delete block CODEC fields and codec overrides from custom blocks.
Move brewing mixes into recipes and declare fuel through the data component.

to: none; output textures are set per RenderPass
note: Create the RenderPass in a try-with-resources and specify its output textures there.

from: QuadCollection#getAll() passed straight to the buffer
to: ItemQuads.split(quads), submitting ItemQuads#solid and #translucent to their phases
note: Wrap item quads in ItemQuads so solid and translucent quads reach the right submit phase.
Providers implement one of the bootstrap interfaces to feed RegistriesDatapackGenerator#forReloadableLayer.
Rework data generation around bootstrap providers instead of a DataProvider subclass.

from: AdvancementProvider taking a list of sub providers directly
to: AdvancementProvider taking List<AdvancementSubProvider$Factory>, with parent references by Identifier only
note: Supply factories that build each AdvancementSubProvider from the BootstrapContext.

from: loot tables, advancements and recipes loaded as non-reloadable registries, slot sources inlined
to: reloadable datapack registries listed in RegistryDataLoader#RELOADABLE_REGISTRIES
note: Expect these entries to reload with the datapack and to be referenced as Holder or HolderSet.

from: SlotSource values only inlined in loot tables
note: Register custom slot sources to the new registry if commands or loot tables should reference them by id.

from: LWJGL built on GLFW, with GLFW key codes
to: LWJGL built on SDL, with different scancode values and SDLScancode
note: Use the constants in InputConstants or SDLScancode instead of hardcoded key codes.
Extend SingleEntryContainerBase for one-entry pools and ExpandableContainerBase for list-like entries.

from: ResourceKey or direct registry value references in reloadable registry code
note: Pick Holder or HolderSet per use case when referencing loot tables, recipes and similar reloadable entries.

to: unknown - no direct rename (tag providers are rebuilt, not renamed)
note: One removal produced 68 errors in Traverse and 97 in Terrestria across four tag-provider files. Treat it as a mechanical rewrite of each provider, not a find-and-replace.
17 of Trinkets 21 errors were this single GUI matrix type change.
4 errors in Trinkets; the knowledge base already covers the CompoundTag -> ValueInput move, so read that entry first.

to: moved packages (take the new owner from the compiler error)
note: 3 moved symbols cost 6 errors in Traveler's Backpack, plus one dead @Shadow target that warned without failing the build. A green build can still ship a dead mixin.

to: unknown - constructor changed; also getProtocolVersion removed and writeCustomData(WriteView) added
note: Polymer: 8 errors, all protocol/constructor shape.
68 of Artifacts 97 errors are inherited generic/override breaks from this refactor. Bumping step by step (1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 -> 1.21.4) is cheaper than one jump.

to: BakedModel -> net.minecraft.client.renderer.block.model.BlockStateModel; ThrownPotion -> ThrownSplashPotion / ThrownLingeringPotion (AbstractThrownPotion is the shared base); CoreShaders -> RenderPipelines, and RenderSystem.setShader takes a RenderPipeline (no POSITION_TEX constant)
note: Read from the 1.21.5 merged jar: no BakedModel, no ThrownPotion, no CoreShaders class exists at all. Traveler's Backpack hits exactly these three.
source: jar listing of minecraft-merged 1.21.5 (loom cache) while repairing Traveler's Backpack
verified: jar contents, not yet compiled against

to: same methods return Optional<T>; use getBooleanOr(k,b), getIntOr(k,i), getLongOr(k,l), getFloatOr(k,f), getShortOr(k,(short)0), getByteOr(k,(byte)0), getStringOr(k,""), getCompoundOrEmpty(k), getListOrEmpty(k)
note: net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag. This one change was ~130 of 196 errors in Traveler's Backpack. The Or(x) helpers reproduce the old absent-key defaults (0 / false / empty string / empty tag), so they are drop-in.

from: CompoundTag#contains(String, int tagType) and CompoundTag#getList(String, int tagType)
to: contains(String) only; getList(String) returning Optional<ListTag> or getListOrEmpty(String)
note: net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag. The 2-arg forms are gone; the element-type check they performed no longer exists.

to: same methods return Optional<T>; use getCompoundOrEmpty(int), getIntOr(i,default), getStringOr(i,""), getListOrEmpty(int)
note: net.minecraft.nbt.ListTag mirrors the CompoundTag change for index access.
net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack. Takes any Tag now and reports failure in the Optional instead of returning an empty stack.

to: ItemStack#save(HolderLookup.Provider) -> Tag (same body: empty stack gives an empty CompoundTag)
note: net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack. The CODEC routes are the longer alternative; save(provider) is the direct rename.

from: MobEffects.MOVEMENT_SLOWDOWN / MOVEMENT_SPEED / DIG_SLOWDOWN / DIG_SPEED / JUMP / CONFUSION / DAMAGE_RESISTANCE
to: MobEffects.SLOWNESS / SPEED / MINING_FATIGUE / HASTE / JUMP_BOOST / NAUSEA / RESISTANCE
note: net.minecraft.world.effect.MobEffects. All are Holder<MobEffect>; the old names no longer exist (they were removed, not deprecated).

Lines are appended with consumer.accept(...). Callers outside an Item pass TooltipDisplay.DEFAULT (and can use stack.getTooltipLines(ctx, player, flag) instead). The TooltipDisplay carries hidden-component state.
net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack. The Level argument was dropped; take it from player.level() if it is still needed.

from: ServerPlayer#setRespawnPosition(ResourceKey<Level>, BlockPos, float angle, boolean forced, boolean sendMessage)
to: ServerPlayer#setRespawnPosition(new ServerPlayer.RespawnConfig(dimension, pos, angle, forced), boolean sendMessage)
note: net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer$RespawnConfig is a record (dimension, pos, angle, forced) that also has a CODEC.

from: BlockBehaviour#onRemove(BlockState, Level, BlockPos, BlockState newState, boolean isMoving)
note: net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour. onRemove no longer exists at all, so the !state.is(newState.getBlock()) guard has no equivalent - the hook only fires on removal. ServerLevel replaces Level.

to: LevelAccessor#updateNeighborsAt(BlockPos, Block) (on Level: updateNeighborsAt(pos, block, Orientation))
note: net.minecraft.world.level.Level. Bed-style placement code (BedBlock.setPlacedBy) is the usual caller; the 2-arg default lives on LevelAccessor.

from: Block#fallOn(Level, BlockState, BlockPos, Entity, float fallDistance)
to: Block#fallOn(Level, BlockState, BlockPos, Entity, double fallDistance)
note: net.minecraft.world.level.block.Block. The override silently stops compiling because the parameter widened to double.

from: BlockEntityRenderer#render(T, float, PoseStack, MultiBufferSource, int light, int overlay)
to: BlockEntityRenderer#render(T, float, PoseStack, MultiBufferSource, int light, int overlay, net.minecraft.world.phys.Vec3 cameraPos)
note: net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer. Every implementation must add the camera position parameter.

from: net.minecraft.client.renderer.item.SelectItemModelProperty with abstract T get(...) and Type type()
note: The Type record and SelectItemModelProperties.ID_MAPPER moved with it. valueCodec() is the codec for the selected value (Codec.INT for an int property).

to: SmithingRecipe#baseIngredient() -> Ingredient (required); templateIngredient() and additionIngredient() stay Optional
note: net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.SmithingRecipe. The default matches() now calls baseIngredient().test(input.base()) unconditionally, so a base-less recipe can no longer pass by default. Ingredient.EMPTY does not exist in 1.21.5, so there is no no-op ingredient to return.
source: javap net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.SmithingRecipe (+ javap -c of the default matches) 1.21.5

to: private; use getNonEquipmentItems() / getItem(int) / setItem(int, ItemStack) / getContainerSize() / getSelectedSlot() / setSelectedSlot(int)
note: net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Inventory. Also Inventory#getSelected() became getSelectedItem(), and the private offhand list is reached with Player#getOffhandItem(). Access widener is the alternative if a mod needs the raw list.

to: PotionContents.addPotionTooltip(Iterable<MobEffectInstance>, Consumer<Component>, float, float) (static), fed by contents.getAllEffects()
note: net.minecraft.world.item.alchemy.PotionContents. It is a static helper now, so the instance receiver becomes the first argument.

to: new DyedItemColor(int color); the record accessor is rgb()
note: net.minecraft.world.item.component.DyedItemColor. The show-in-tooltip flag moved to TooltipDisplay.withHidden.

from: SoundEvents.SHIELD_BLOCK as SoundEvent, usable directly in Level#playSound(Entity, BlockPos, SoundEvent, ...)
to: SoundEvents.SHIELD_BLOCK is Holder.Reference<SoundEvent>; call .value() for the SoundEvent overloads (the Holder overload exists only for the double x/y/z form)
note: net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvents / net.minecraft.world.level.Level. Only some constants became holders, so this surfaces as a single no-suitable-method error rather than a rename sweep.

from: EntityModel<T extends Entity> / HumanoidModel<T extends LivingEntity>
to: EntityModel<T extends EntityRenderState> / HumanoidModel<T extends HumanoidRenderState>
note: The render-state refactor landed in 1.21.2. A model used outside the vanilla entity renderer (e.g. an armor-style artifact) must be parameterised with a render state it fills itself; the entity is no longer a type parameter.

from: setupAnim(T entity, float limbSwing, float limbSwingAmount, float ageInTicks, float netHeadYaw, float headPitch) and prepareMobModel(...)
to: setupAnim(T state) only; interpolation happens when the render state is extracted
note: HumanoidModel.setupAnim reads left/rightArmPose, swimAmount, isFallFlying, xRot/yRot, walkAnimationPos/Speed, speedValue, isPassenger, mainArm, isUsingItem, useItemHand, ageInTicks, isCrouching, attackArm, attackTime, ageScale, maxCrossbowChargeDuration, ticksUsingItem. Fill every one, or setupAttackAnimation/poseArm null-derefs.

from: override renderToBuffer(PoseStack, VertexConsumer, int light, int overlay, int color) on a Model subclass
to: Model.renderToBuffer(...) is final; hide parts with ModelPart.visible (setAllVisible(false)) or push/scale the PoseStack at the call site
note: ModelPart.copyFrom (used by HumanoidModel.copyPropertiesTo) copies scale, rotation and position but NOT visible, so hidden-part models survive follow-body rotations.

from: Model.headParts() / Model.bodyParts() and the Model.young field
to: per-part ModelPart.visible flags; baby-ness is HumanoidRenderState.isBaby
note: Rendering walks the whole model root now, so a single-piece model must switch the other humanoid parts invisible in its constructor.

from: HumanoidModel.leftArmPose / rightArmPose / crouching / attackTime / swimAmount fields
note: Setting an arm pose from an event now means mutating the render state during extractRenderState, not the model after extraction.

from: EntityRenderer.render(T entity, float yaw, float partialTicks, PoseStack, MultiBufferSource, int) and LivingEntityRenderer.getTextureLocation(T)
to: render(S state, PoseStack, MultiBufferSource, int), getTextureLocation(S), plus createRenderState() and extractRenderState(T, S, float)
note: MobRenderer is now MobRenderer<T, S, M>. Per-entity data a layer needs (a mimic's ticksInAir, a chosen chest material) must be copied into the state during extractRenderState, because render and layer code only sees the state.

from: RenderLayer<S extends Entity, M extends EntityModel<S>> and render(..., S entity, float limbSwing, float limbSwingAmount, float partialTicks, float ageInTicks, float netHeadYaw, float headPitch)
to: RenderLayer<S extends EntityRenderState, M extends EntityModel<? super S>> and render(PoseStack, MultiBufferSource, int light, S state, float limbSwing, float limbSwingAmount)
note: No entity and no partial ticks inside a layer any more; bake interpolated values into the state at extraction time.
Passing a render-state model to a HumanoidModel copy needs a raw cast when the type arguments differ; the copy is per ModelPart so it stays safe.

from: Entity.hurt(DamageSource, float), overridable and returning boolean
to: Entity.hurtServer(ServerLevel, DamageSource, float) overridable; hurt(DamageSource, float) is final void
note: Damage code calls entity.hurtServer(serverLevel, source, amount); the old boolean return now comes from hurtServer.
Only reachable through a LivingEntity cast; Entity no longer resolves the one-arg form.

to: net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult (SUCCESS/CONSUME/FAIL/PASS); Item.use(Level, Player, InteractionHand) returns InteractionResult
note: InteractionResultHolder.consume(stack) becomes InteractionResult.CONSUME and .pass(stack) becomes InteractionResult.PASS.
Item.getUseAnimation(ItemStack) returns ItemUseAnimation; EAT/DRINK/BLOCK are unchanged.
Cooldowns are keyed by the stack's cooldown-group component, so every call site must pass the stack it already holds.

to: item model definitions: assets/<ns>/items/<name>.json with minecraft:condition + minecraft:using_item (was a custom 'artifacts:blocking' property)
note: 1.21.4 deleted the item-property registry; there is no Java-side replacement, only data. Fabric API 0.119.2 also dropped net.fabricmc.fabric.api.renderer.v1 (ForwardingBakedModel/RenderContext), so a BakedModel wrapper can no longer swap a model per display context.
Mechanical; both bounds come from LevelHeightAccessor now.
ContextKey moved to net.minecraft.util.context.ContextKey; the methods were renamed with it.
The selector gained the ServerLevel argument, so an existing lambda fails with 'incompatible parameter types in lambda expression'.

to: Minecraft.getDeltaTracker(); Item.getName(); GuiGraphics.blit(Function<ResourceLocation, RenderType>, ResourceLocation, ...) e.g. RenderType::guiTextured
note: Three unrelated renames that land together in the same bump; the blit overload no longer accepts a raw texture id as its first argument.

to: Registry.get / BuiltInRegistries.X.get return Optional<Holder.Reference<T>> (use getValue for the value); RegistryAccess.lookup(...); tags via getTags()/getTagOrEmpty/getRandomElementOf(TagKey, RandomSource)
note: The tag helpers disappeared outright: there is no getTag(TagKey) on Registry any more, only a stream of HolderSet.Named plus getRandomElementOf.

to: ServerLevel.recipeAccess() (a RecipeManager); recipe.assemble(RecipeInput, HolderLookup.Provider) for the result; AbstractCookingRecipe.experience()
note: Level.recipeAccess() only exposes RecipeAccess (stonecutter + property sets), so recipe lookups need the ServerLevel covariant return.
Consumable.onConsume applies FoodProperties and the consume effects and fires the use event, which is what ItemStack.finishUsingItem now does.

to: EntityType.create(Level, EntitySpawnReason); Builder.build(ResourceKey<EntityType<?>>); the loot table comes from that key (entities/<path>)
note: The key passed to build() now also determines the default loot table, so a custom getDefaultLootTable override is both impossible and unnecessary.
Same behaviour, now a public singleton instead of a field on ArmorItem.

from: MobEffect.applyEffectTick(LivingEntity, int); LightningBolt.create(Level); SpawnEggItem(type, int, int, Properties)
to: MobEffect.applyEffectTick(ServerLevel, LivingEntity, int); EntityType.LIGHTNING_BOLT.create(Level, EntitySpawnReason); SpawnEggItem(type, Properties)
note: The spawn-egg colours are gone (they come from the entity's spawn egg data), and ticking effects receive the ServerLevel.
Fabric API 0.119.2 for 1.21.4 changed the resource-condition lookup type; an unchanged override stops compiling and the class silently stops being a ResourceCondition.
